articles.headline: Zero Escape Writer Is Pro-AI, Believes His New Studio’s Game Wouldn’t Have Been Canceled If He’d Used It To Cut Costs
keyFacts: Game developer Kotaro Uchikoshi stated that his new studio Crash Keys suffered the cancellation of its first game, marking one of his worst days as a developer.
Uchikoshi said the game might not have been canceled if he had used artificial intelligence to cut costs and reduce development time.
Uchikoshi expressed support for proactive artificial intelligence use in game development to refine tasks and help creators reach their full vision.
body: The reputation that Kotaro Uchikoshi has developed for surreal and metatextual storytelling through games like Hundred Line: Final Defense Academy and the Zero Escape series means that it can be difficult to know when heâs being entirely forthright and serious. For instance, when he announced his new studio called Crash Keys by telling the world the game he was working on at the company had been canceled, people were more likely to believe it was an ARG than the truth. Yet in a new interview, he insists the studio and its game’s cancellation were real, and says that maybe the game wouldnât have been canceled if he had been allowed to use AI.

But why start a new studio? He sat down with Famitsu to discuss it, telling the publication it was partially to make more âUchikoshi-likeâ games while still working with his friends and partners at Danganronpa creator Kazutaka Kodakaâs Too Kyo Games. âEven if someone thinks ‘I want to work with Uchikoshi,’ the fact Iâm affiliated with Too Kyo Games makes it harder for them to reach out. More, they feel cautious about it, and frame their request to work with me in a way that also takes Kodaka and the studio into consideration. I ultimately felt that if I wanted to collaborate more with people interested in funding a project thatâs distinctly ‘Uchikoshi’ in style, or simply wanted to work with me, it would be better to have my own studio that serves my personal identity.â

The cancellation of the game previously in development at Crash Keys, he explains, was among his worst days as a developer. After a meeting with his publisher that confirmed the news, he commented on his personal social media account that he may not have had to cancel the project had he been able to use AI to cut costs and reduce development time, thoughts he expanded on in the interview.

âWhen it comes to the state of the current games industry, I really feel that AI is playing a huge role,â Uchikoshi explains. âFor mid-sized teams like ours, especially those making adventure games, even indie games created by individuals could now be seen as rivals. Some of these individuals are using AI with very small teams to produce expansive games with rich content in a short time at a low cost. When compared to their budget and development times, itâs very difficult for a mid-sized studio to compete. So what should we do? I believe we have no choice but to use AI ourselves.

âI understand thereâs resistance to using AI in game development. However, personally, I am a proponent of AI, and I believe we should be more proactive about using it to make games. I donât think AI diminishes human creativity in any form. When it comes to visual design such as illustrations and graphics, design, and of course story, the origin and inspiration must come from human ideas. However, when it comes to the subsequent steps, such as refining and polishing that, Iâm perfectly okay with entrusting that task to AI to some extent. By using AI this way, I think it actually brings creators closer to realizing what they want to make.

“For example, if you ask a staff member to make a graphic adjustment and give instructions to move something by a few dots, you may start by asking them to move it 10 dots, but realize when you see the revised version it doesnât look right. So you tell them, actually, move it 5 dots to the right, and when they fix it, realize immediately that, you know, maybe it should be 3 dots. If you keep going back and forth three or four times, they will lose their patience and their motivation will drop. But AI can handle that endlessly without a single complaint. So, if previously a final product may be 70-80 percent of a creatorâs vision, this can bring it as close to 100 percent of what they creator initially envisioned.â

In his view, it may also reduce game development time in an era where even five years is quick. If, with the help of AI, it takes only half that time, it may not mean you cut staff, but it may mean you can work on another project in that time instead, one also fueled by AI. So, he doesnât view it in a negative light, despite the concerns of players.
Previously, Uchikoshi said Hundred Line may be âone of the last timesâ a game of that scale would be made without AI. It seems he is willing to actively ensure that statement proves true.

articles.headline: Fantasy Football D/ST Rankings: Week 8 2026
keyFacts: Yahoo Sports released fantasy football defense and special teams rankings for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season.
The Cincinnati Bengals, Los Angeles Rams, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Jacksonville Jaguars are highlighted as top fantasy defensive options for the week.
Byes in Week 8 include the Texans, 49ers, Saints, and Giants.
body: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Fantasy Football D/ST Rankings: Week 8 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The fantasy football season nears the halfway point. And some players are still proving their worth . But looking ahead, here are the fantasy football defense and special teams rankings for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season.

It’s another week where the byes come into play. The Texans, although they’ve been very disappointing, are off. Also taking a rest are the 49ers, Saints, and Giants. And that leaves some interesting teams at the top.
Fantasy Football standouts

It’s a good week to take a chance on the Bengals. They have a great matchup against the offensive emptiness of the Titans. In full fairness, the Titans showed a little bit of life against the Browns in a 27-24 loss in Week 7.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
But the Bengals really showed their teeth. They gave up 13 first-half points to the Ravens, but shut them down the rest of the way. Along the way, they had four sacks and an interception.
Edge rusher Boye Mafe has made a big difference for this Bengals defense, according to Pro Football Focus.

“Mafe starred against the Ravens, producing an initial 90.2 overall PFF grade — a mark that would set a new career high,” Bradley Locker wrote. “His impact was most felt as a pass-rusher, generating five pressures and two sacks on a gaudy 23.1% pass-rush win rate over 27 pass-rushing snaps.

“Mafe’s career-best outing in Week 7 punctuates what’s been a revelatory season for the first-year Bengals. Through seven weeks, Mafe has produced an 88.9 overall PFF grade, the fourth-highest among edge rushers to play 200 or more snaps this season.”
Another strong point for the Bengals has been their red zone work. They rank No. 3 in the NFL, allowing only 35% of opportunities to result in touchdowns, according to cleveland.com.

“I think they’re playing with a lot of confidence,” Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said. “It’s calls we review every week and do a really good job walking through, trying to practice them on Fridays, what we’re gonna do.”
And they succeeded against the Ravens despite being on the field a lot.

“Sometimes it’s after long drives where you’ve been on the field yesterday for eight minutes,” Taylor said. “And it’s defeating because they’ve converted third downs and gotten big plays. And you got to overcome adversity, and then you got to just buckle up and hold them to a field goal. That’s what we did twice yesterday. And that turned out to be really significant in the first half to hold them to those field goals and not touchdowns.”

As for the Titans, Tony Pollard is coming off a big game with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns. Don’t look for Pollard to be able to repeat that type of performance against the Bengals. That’s true even though the Bengals have been below average against the run, ranking No. 18 with 116.3 yards allowed per game.

As high on the list are the Rams. They get a home game against the struggling Chargers. The Chargers rank No. 27 in the NFL with just 287.2 yards per game. They’ve struggled to get quarterback Justin Herbert rolling.
And the Rams seemed to find something on both sides of the ball last week against the Raiders.
Unfortunately, the Rams still don’t know when Myles Garrett will be back on the field, according to a post on X by Nate Atkins.
“The Rams have not made a determination yet on whether or not to open the practice windows for Myles Garrett or Terrance Ferguson, per Sean McVay.”
Even without Garrett, the Rams should have a shot at making some splash fantasy plays against the Chargers.
Other standouts
The Steelers’ defense has been solid if nothing else. And they have a good matchup against the Browns this week. It should be a low-scoring game.
They are coming off a game where they held the Saints to 18 yards on 17 carries. Confidence is brimming , according to Post-Gazette.com.

“We have a lot of confidence in creating turnovers and creating those splash plays,” said outside linebacker T.J. Watt. “We’ve done a really good job trying not to press too hard to make those plays happen, and they’ve been coming to us.”
The Browns have been one of the most surprising teams in the NFL. But this could be the week the offense gets overwhelmed and can’t keep up.

Another good fantasy pick this week is the Jaguars. They’re coming off a bye week and have a matchup against the shaky Colts’ offense. If they can keep Jonathan Taylor from cutting loose, they have a shot to make plays when the Colts pass the football.
Overall, the opportunity is there , according to rotoballer.com.

“The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST has one of the best matchups of the week,” Joey Pollizze wrote. “The Colts have had a hard time moving the ball this season. They rank 25th in EPA/play, 20th in points per game, and 24th in sacks allowed per game. Daniel Jones has also thrown an interception in six of seven contests, and Indianapolis has been held to under 24 points in four of the last five weeks.”
Fantasy Football sleepers

Oh, you have to be brave to go here. But the Commanders have a nice matchup against an inept Eagles offense. With Saquon Barkley pulling up gimpy against the Cowboys on Monday, the Eagles can’t exactly throw a scare into the Commanders.

What you’re banking on is a good sack effort. The Commanders have been able to get better pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. But they haven’t finished a lot, with only 11 sacks on the season.

Another sleeper pick is the Browns. They get the Steelers this week. That’s not a great matchup, but Aaron Rodgers is immobile. If the Browns can get pressure, they have a chance for a strong fantasy outing.

articles.headline: Why Brandon Miller is ready to become the new face of the Charlotte Hornets
keyFacts: Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points and hit the game-clinching shot in the Charlotte Hornets' 110-103 victory over the Washington Wizards.
Miller, the team's new focal point after signing a five-year, $209 million contract extension, also purchased 500 tickets for breast cancer survivors.
Charlotte coach Charles Lee and teammate Moussa Diabate said the team fully trusts Miller to make plays.
body: As the franchise's new face, Brandon Miller is fully aware of his responsibilities.
The Charlotte Hornets’ fourth-year swingman made sure to handle them Monday night in a variety of ways, doing it on and off the court.

Miller purchased 500 tickets for breast cancer survivors to attend the Hornets’ matchup with the Washington Wizards — “I was really going to do more, a lot more than that,” he said — and then went out and put on a show. By tossing in a career-best 39 points, hitting the game-clinching bucket and leaving his imprints all over Charlotte’s 110-103 victory at Spectrum Center, Miller couldn’t have scripted it any better.

In flashing his two-way ability to propel Charlotte (3-1) to a third win in four games despite missing Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams with injuries, Miller stuffed the stat sheet to an impressive tune. He was also a force defensively, collecting a pair of steals and two blocked shots. One of those was of the chase-down variety, running full court and swatting just enough of Bub Carrington’s layup prior to it reaching the glass.

“Just the motivation side,” Miller said of what drives him to be an all-around player for the Hornets. “My teammates motivate me a lot. It just builds my confidence to go out there and make every winning play that I can.
“So whatever winning play it is, I’m going to do my best to make it.”
Brian Westerholt-Imagn Images

Miller’s signature is fully dry on the hefty five-year, $209 million rookie-scale contract extension he signed on Oct. 21, not long before the deadline. With LaMelo Ball now in Minnesota and Miles Bridges in Phoenix, Miller steps into the seat as the Hornets’ longest-tenured player.
The bull’s-eye is squarely on him and he’s not shying from it. In fact, he’s receiving assurances from his teammates. Whether it’s Knueppel, White, Naz Reid, Grayson Allen or anyone else.

“They’re like, ‘You are that guy, we believe in you,’” Hornets coach Charles Lee said. “‘So when we put the ball in your hand, go make a play. For yourself, for your teammates.’ Not only is Brandon prepared for it, but his teammates want to see him in those moments and they encourage him in those moments, which is really helping as well.”
Count Moussa Diabate among them.

“We all trust him with the ball,” Diabate said. “That’s the whole reason why he got paid. At the end of the day, there’s no second thoughts for who’s getting the ball. Whether he makes it or misses it, we’ll be right with him. For our entire team, our entire organization, we trust him with the ball. No matter it is.”
Miller doesn’t take that for granted, either. Not one bit.

“It makes you smile every day, just to see other NBA guys put all their trust in me,” said Miller, who reached 500 made career 3-pointers in the second-fewest games in NBA history. “But at the same time I have to trust those guys. I have to go to war for those guys every night, too, and vice versa. They are going to go to work for me.
“So just being ready when the time comes, the preparation that we put in being ready and staying ready. It goes a long way in our season and games like this.”

Similar to why Miller makes it a mission to mingle with patrons, team employees and whoever else may cross his path following his pre-game shooting routine for home games. He always stops and chats with a few people before heading back into the locker room, often signing several autographs and posing for selfies.

“It started my rookie year,” Miller said. “Whether it’s ball girl, ball boy, fans. Security here, whoever the case may be, just trying to build a bond just in case. They’re always going to try to go to war for me while I’m on the court playing, so I think it’s kind of a must for me to know who is all going to war for me and who I want to go to war with.”

articles.headline: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
keyFacts: Apple unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip, starting at $1,999.
Apple also announced a new iMac powered by the M6 chip, starting at $1,499.
Both new devices are available for preorder starting October 28 and launch on November 6.
body: Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver.

Apple also announced its latest iMac, which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini.

The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip.
The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says.
The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip.
It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera.
The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter.

As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production.
The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver.

The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27.
Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6.

articles.headline: Everything Apple announced this week so far: New iPad and MacBooks
keyFacts: Apple announced new hardware ahead of its Pro and Tell event, including an OLED iPad mini, an M6 iMac, and a 14-inch MacBook Pro.
The new eighth-generation OLED iPad mini starts at $699 with pre-orders opening October 28 and retail availability on November 6.
Apple released new operating system versions with updated Siri AI features and updated Apple Creator Studio with new creative tools.
body: Everything Apple announced this week so far: New iPad and MacBooks
Ahead of its 'Pro and Tell' event, the company has already launched a few new devices.

Apple wasn't done with its product reveals for the fall after unveiling the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro models and an array of smart home devices. Nor could it wait until the third event of the season, dubbed Pro and Tell, to show off more gear.

The company got a string of announcements underway on Monday with the reveal of the long-awaited OLED iPad mini. Tuesday brought us an M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro. It's expected that Apple will unveil a touchscreen MacBook as well.

Elsewhere, Apple released the latest versions of its operating systems. Among other things, those added more Siri AI features and made the assistant available in more languages. The company updated Apple Creator Studio with more AI features and creative tools as well.
We'll update this story if and when Apple makes more announcements. In the meantime, here's everything Apple has announced so far this week.
OLED iPad mini

It feels like we've been waiting for forever for Apple to put an OLED display in the iPad mini but that day has finally arrived. The new display has double the peak brightness of the one on the previous model at 1,200 nits, and it has a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The base storage remains the same at 128GB, though if you opt for 256GB or 512GB of storage, you can snag a variant with a nano-texture glass display. That'll cost you extra, naturally.

The company managed to squeeze in a larger screen — an 8.5-inch display rather than the 8.3-inch one in the previous model — without increasing the size of the tablet. In fact, the new iPad mini is slightly narrower than the last one, at 5.22 inches vs. 5.3 inches. It's lighter as well, with the Wi-Fi model coming in at 0.56 pounds (compared with 0.65 pounds last time) and the 5G variant weighing 0.58 pounds (versus 0.66 pounds). The latter, by the way, now boasts Apple's C2 modem, which is said to deliver up to 50 percent faster data speeds than the previous iPad mini. There's also Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity thanks to the N1 chip.

The OLED iPad mini — the eighth generation of the device — runs on the A20 Pro, the same chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Apple says the SoC is capable of running large language models locally, in case you're into that kind of thing. Otherwise, the tablet should be notably faster than earlier models. It supports Apple Intelligence and Siri AI as well, of course. The chipset also boasts a 7-core GPU — two more cores than the A17 Pro, which powered the last-gen iPad mini.

On the camera front, there's a 12MP Center Stage lens on front of the tablet, which Apple has finally shifted to the landscape edge on the iPad mini. However, there's still no Face ID. The 12MP camera on the rear supports 4K 60fps video capture and Smart HDR 4.

The 8th-gen iPad mini has a sealed enclosure to help protect it from the elements. The tablet has an IP67 rating, meaning that it should withstand dust and being immersed in a meter of freshwater for up to 30 minutes, though I would advise against intentionally submerging your iPad mini.

As for battery life, Apple says that should be roughly the same as last time. The company says the new iPad mini should run for up to 10 hours when you're watching video or surfing the web over Wi-Fi. That drops down to nine hours if you're browsing over a cellular connection. If you have at least a 35W power adaptor, you'll be able to recharge the battery to 50 percent of its capacity in 30 minutes, Apple says.

The most interesting thing to me about this iPad mini is that it has Apple's first Acoustic Display, which the company says helps it deliver "an even better audio experience." It claims the tablet offers more volume and "punchier bass" thanks to woofers that "are paired through the display." Apple added that "custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs." I'm definitely curious to find out how all of that sounds in practice.

Inevitably, the latest iPad mini comes with a price hike. It starts at $699, which is $150 more than the previous model after Apple increased the price of that in June. Pre-orders open on October 28, and the tablet will hit shelves on November 6.
M6 iMac
On Tuesday, Apple gave the iMac and MacBook Pro spec bumps. The desktop and laptop now each have the M6 chipset, which recently debuted in the Mac mini.

Let's start with the new iMac. Apple says the M6's dual 16-core neural engine enables it to deliver up to five times faster on-device AI performance (for Siri AI, Apple Intelligence and local LLMs) than the previous-gen iMac from 2024, which had the M4 chipset. The M6 is said to deliver up to 1.5 times faster performance than the M4 for daily tasks, up to two times faster graphics performance (for photo editing etc.) and up to two times higher gaming performance with ray tracing.

The base-level M6 has 10 CPU cores (two super, three performance and two efficiency cores) and a 10-core CPU, compared with eight of each in the M4. There's the option to have a 12-core M6, in which case your desktop will have four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of the two that the base model has. The four-port model has a nano-texture glass option as well.

Elsewhere, Apple has introduced its N1 networking chip to the iMac. As such, the computer has support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity. It also has the option to add a 2.5Gb Ethernet port, an upgrade from gigabit Ethernet on the M4 iMac.

Specs otherwise are the same as last time. You'll still get a 24-inch 4.5K Super Retina display, a 12MP Center Stage camera, a six‑speaker Dolby Atmos system, at least 16GB of RAM and 256GB of base storage. The dimensions are identical too, though the M6 iMac is a touch lighter than the previous gen at 9.7 pounds (versus 9.74 pounds). Don't expect any changes to the color options either — the new iMac is still available in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver.

One other thing that's staying the same? The starting price, at least after the $200 increase that Apple gave the M4 iMac over the summer. The new model starts at $1,499, and the four-port version will run you at least $1,699. Pre-orders open October 28 and you'll be able to pick one up in store on November 6.
M6 14-inch MacBook Pro
The latest 14-inch MacBook Pro has the 12-core version of the M6 chipset and the N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. Those appear to be the only spec changes this time.

Compared with the previous-gen 14-inch MBP, which had an M5 SoC, Apple says the M6 model offers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads. It's said to deliver up to 1.3 faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender, up to 1.2 times faster image-processing performance in Affinity and up to 1.3 faster project build performance for compiling code in Xcode.

It doesn't seem like this will be a massive upgrade for folks with an M5 model. However, if you have an older MacBook Pro (or really need those incremental improvements from the previous gen), it might be worth making the switch.

At least you won't have to pay more than you would have for the M5 model following this summer's price increase. The M6-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 for 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. Again, pre-orders start on Wednesday with general availability to follow on November 6.

articles.headline: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
keyFacts: The leaders of Finland and Norway held a joint call with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss ending the war in Ukraine.
Finnish and Norwegian leaders said the war's outcome directly impacts European security, while Putin blamed NATO policies for prolonging it.
Putin and the Nordic leaders agreed to continue direct communication, as partners prepare for upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi.
body: - Published
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.

The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".
After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.
The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.
Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", StÃ¸re said.

Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".
StÃ¸re added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
He - like Stubb and StÃ¸re - had agreed to continue their direct phone communication, the statement added.
StÃ¸re said all their allies had been informed of the call ahead of time.
Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "very sceptical" of Tuesday's dialogue, telling Danish broadcaster DR, it had not been "co-ordinated with any of the rest of us".
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates, was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US, Ukraine and its European allies have been souring since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia - allowing it to export oil to the US.
But last week, Stubb, StÃ¸re and Zelesnky met with Witkoff in the Norwegian capital, before the US special envoy travelled on to St Petersburg to meet Putin.
Following the talks, Ukraine, Russia and the US agreed to resume three-way negotiations that Russia had stopped for months.
After speaking to the two Nordic leaders, Zelensky said part of their discussions with Putin had centred on November's trilateral talks to be held in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky said he had discussed with them "various formats for our engagement with partners in Europe that could be useful in further supporting diplomacy, our defense, and our shared security".
Stubb and StÃ¸re are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
As the US administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the European Union of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".

articles.headline: Nvidia may not have discontinued the RTX 5090, but one AIB partner says it can't get hold of the parts required to make the card
keyFacts: An Nvidia AIB partner stated they cannot purchase the GB202 GPU and GDDR7 memory set required to manufacture the RTX 5090 graphics card.
Nvidia confirmed the RTX 5090 has not been discontinued, though the company acknowledged that limited supply chain capacity has constrained output.
A cooler manufacturer reported that partners reduced order forecasts for RTX 5090 heatsinks for early 2027 due to ongoing supply issues.
body: Nvidia's RTX 5090 has been a subject of much speculation recently, as it was rumoured to be discontinued last month when it vanished from the company's official marketplace, only for Nvidia to confirm it wasn't discontinued. The plot has thickened, though, as AIB partners—the companies actually designing and manufacturing RTX 50 series graphics cards—suggest even they can't get their hands on the parts required to make the card.

This is according to an Nvidia AIB partner who spoke to YouTuber Der8auer. They say, "No, Nvidia did not inform us that RTX 5090 is EOL. But currently we cannot purchase GB202 [the GPU] together with 32 GB GDDR7 as [a] complete set, and we also don't know if ordering will be possible again in the future."
The unnamed board partner clarifies that in previous shortages, they could place backorders with Nvidia, but this is "currently not possible anymore."

This is all to say that this AIB partner is unable to get the GPU and memory required to make the RTX 5090, and doesn't know when that supply issue will be fixed. Though this isn't the card being discontinued, for many partners, not getting the GPU and VRAM is as good as doing so.
Whether it's the GPU or the memory that's causing the biggest headache isn't specified, though in the current context, one can assume it's likely both to some degree.

As of right now, companies are reliant on GPU and VRAM bundles from Nvidia before they can make their own cards. There have previously been rumours that Nvidia would stop bundling its GPUs and VRAM together, but even if it did that, this would only partly solve the issue of the memory crisis for Nvidia. Those who might have been able to buy just the GPU would still be subject to a price squeeze on the VRAM when trying to source it direct from one of the major memory manufacturers.

Der8auer also spoke to an RTX 5090 cooler manufacturer who said, "Two of our partners already reduced quite much the order forecast for RTX 5090 based heatsinks in Q1 2027, when compare[d] with Q3 2026."

"For Q2 2027, until now we still did not receive any order for RTX 5090 model heatsinks from our partners."

Nvidia still remains steadfast in saying the card has not been discontinued, though it acknowledges that limited supply chain capacity has led to a "somewhat constrained" output. Its German branch says, "Nvidia will continue to ship it, and this is very important."

The RTX 5090 (an already expensive card at its previous MSRP of $2,000) has been prohibitively expensive for months. It's so pricey, in fact, that we stopped tracking it in our graphics card price watch. It has been incredibly difficult to find any of the cards available from reputable sellers at even reasonable prices (with some listed for upwards of $8,000 right now) and therefore we could never recommend actually picking one up. Though it may not be officially discontinued, it seems like the likelihood of picking one up soon at a decent price is getting slimmer and slimmer by the day.

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.

articles.headline: Rumors continue to fly about Nvidia's RTX 5090 GPU stock shortages
keyFacts: Laptop maker XMG warned that prices for RTX 5090 laptops will increase significantly due to constrained component availability and a RAM crisis.
An unnamed graphics-card maker told overclocker Der8auer that it cannot currently purchase the GB203 chip and VRAM package or place backorders from Nvidia.
Nvidia has firmly denied that the RTX 5090 has been discontinued, despite severe supply shortages affecting both desktop and laptop versions.
body: - XMG warns that 'substantial price increases for upcoming GPU shipments' mean it's hiking RTX 5090 laptop prices
- One model is already pricier and bigger hikes for XMG's other notebooks could be coming soon
- At the same time, we're hearing more about the struggles of Nvidia's partners for supply of components for the desktop RTX 5090

The position of Nvidia's RTX 5090 is looking shakier by the day, as even more chatter is emerging suggesting that this GPU is effectively sidelined at this point, even if it hasn't actually been discontinued.
You may have read up on those recent rumors claiming that Nvidia has discontinued the RTX 5090 — which is speculation that Team Green has firmly denied, I should make clear.
The fresh negative news from the grapevine comes firstly from laptop maker XMG on Reddit, which is sharing more bad news on the RAM crisis affecting its prices, specifically with the RTX 5090.
XMG says: "We expect laptops with the RTX 5090 to become significantly more expensive again over the coming weeks." (We already saw price hikes from XMG last month, if you recall).

The company explains why: "Procurement conditions for the RTX 5090 Laptop GPU have deteriorated considerably within a short period. We have received new information indicating substantial price increases for upcoming GPU shipments.

"At the same time, availability is becoming increasingly constrained. Replenishment orders that have already been planned or, in some cases, even confirmed are being significantly reduced in quantity."
XMG notes that beyond these existing orders, it is "currently difficult to make reliable predictions about future supply volumes and delivery dates."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

The laptop maker also tells us that "other laptop GPUs are also facing supply constraints", but that the "combination of massive price increases and extremely limited supply" is "particularly pronounced" with the RTX 5090.

That doesn't sound very comforting, does it? The immediate result is that the Schenker Key 18 Pro laptop (Schenker is XMG's parent company) with the RTX 5090 has increased in price by €250 (around $280 / £210 / AU$400) as of today, and the XMG NEO laptops with the RTX 5090 will see at least a similar price increase — although we're warned that the "increase could be even higher" for those notebooks depending on how the situation develops. Nasty.
The second shot of negativity here is from overclocker Der8auer in Germany, who as Wccftech reports, has heard from one of Nvidia's board making partners.

Add seasoning as appropriate here, but the unnamed graphics-card maker claims that while it hasn't been informed that the RTX 5090 is discontinued — Nvidia Germany also told Der8auer this (backing up other statements to this effect from Team Green) — it cannot currently purchase the GB203 chip plus VRAM package (32GB of GDDR7 video RAM) to make the RTX 5090 laptop card.

The more worrying part is that the board maker says that this kind of component shortage has happened before, but it has always been able to place a backorder to be fulfilled later. However, right now it's not even possible to obtain a backorder from Nvidia.

A maker of coolers for the RTX 5090 further observes that it has witnessed reduced orders from board makers, and it doesn't have any orders at all for heatsinks for Nvidia's flagship GPU for Q2 2027 at this point. That obviously suggests that the production quantities for the RTX 5090 are looking even shakier for the future.
Analysis: bleak times
At some point, the accumulation of rumors begins to reach a kind of critical mass where it seems very unlikely that they're all off base, and that in all likelihood, something really is going on.

We appear to be arriving at this point with the RTX 5090 rumors, in my opinion. There are too many of them, and the indications at the retail level — vanishing stock, and ever-increasing RTX 5090 prices, which have become truly ridiculous — also back up the grapevine here.

What's worrying is the further gloom from the likes of a cooler manufacturer, and the fact that the RTX 5090 laptop GPU is also involved. Remember that this doesn't use the GB202 chip seen in the desktop RTX 5090, but Nvidia's GB203 silicon; however, the supply problem lies in getting the video RAM (3GB GDDR7 modules, which are now thinner on the ground and far pricier than the 2GB modules used in the RTX 5080 laptop graphics card).

So, while the RTX 5090 may not be discontinued, it would appear that supplies are getting so low for this GPU — on both desktop and laptop fronts — that while technically it's still in production, the quantities are dipping to such an extent that the flagship is effectively being pushed aside.
All in all, it feels like an especially bleak time for higher-end Nvidia graphics cards, and the fear is that the situation may worsen from here.

Certainly when we look at the predictions for the RAM crisis next year, they're universally pessimistic, and there's a greater level of belief these days that memory supply woes could last for the rest of this decade. Of course, VRAM is bound up in that, as well as AI demand for GPU chips, and all this could affect the launch timeframe of Nvidia's next-gen GeForce graphics cards, too.

articles.headline: Feds raid billionaire’s Beverly Hills mansion as Eric Swalwell probe takes another dramatic twist
keyFacts: The FBI raided a Beverly Hills mansion linked to billionaire Stephen Cloobeck as part of an ongoing investigation into former politician Eric Swalwell.
Swalwell faces multiple allegations of sexual assault and misconduct from former staffers and other women, leading to his resignation and withdrawal from a gubernatorial race.
Investigators previously seized Swalwell's electronic devices under a federal civil-rights statute exploring whether he abused his government power to silence accusers.
body: The FBI on Tuesday morning raided a Beverly Hills mansion as part of the investigation into disgraced California politician Eric Swalwell.
The raid is believed to have targeted the home of billionaire Stephen Cloobeck, who prominently backed Swalwell’s run for governor and even let him stay at his mansion in Southern California.
However, when allegations surfaced that former Congressman Swalwell sexually assaulted mutlple women including former staffers, Cloobeck changed his mind and reportedly evicted him out of the house.
“I am no longer associated with a man that takes advantage of women,” Cloobeck said. “I support women’s rights.”
Swalwell is under investigation by multiple prosecutors for the sexual assault allegations, including in New York and California.

Back in August, Swalwell was surrounded by FBI agents at San Francisco International Airport as he deboarded a plane, leading to the seizure of his cellphone and laptop as part of a federal criminal investigation.
Agents executed additional warrants the following day at Swalwell’s Washington, D.C., home, where they seized other potential evidence, a source previously told The Post.

The FBI warrant used to seize Swalwell’s phone and laptop cited a federal civil-rights statute that can be used to prosecute public officials who abuse their government power — suggesting the feds may suspect Swalwell used his official role to silence women who accused him of sexual misconduct.

One former staffer has accused Swalwell of raping her when she was too intoxicated to consent, according to the San Francisco Chronicle. Another woman has accused him of drugging and sexually assaulting her in 2018, while two others have alleged he sent them unsolicited images of his genitals.
Swalwell has denied wrongdoing, but he dropped out of the governor’s race and resigned from Congress soon after the allegations surfaced.

Cloobeck was one of Swalwell’s largest benefactors, spending over $1 million to support Swalwell’s California gubernatorial campaign, giving the maximum $39,200 direct contribution, and providing a private $31,000 trip to France in 2024.
Swalwell frequently lived and stayed out of Cloobeck’s Beverly Hills mansion, even filming a video response to misconduct allegations from inside the home.
Cloobeck himself ran for governor before dropping out to make way for Swalwell.
The benefactor, while he now disavows Swalwell, has had troubles of his own. He was about to marry a Penthouse Pet accused of stealing from rich sugar daddies before calling it off.

Cloobeck was charged with three felony counts of attempting to dissuade or prevent a witness or victim from testifying, and one misdemeanor count of making annoying phone calls. All charges stem from his ex-partner Adva Lavie’s criminal case in which she’s accused of using dating apps to steal from rich older men.

articles.headline: UFC Pound-for-Pound Fighter Rankings: Alexander Volkanovski and Petr Yan shine at UFC 333
keyFacts: Alexander Volkanovski defeated Movsar Evloev by second-round TKO at UFC 333 to break the UFC record for featherweight title wins.
Petr Yan used calm midfight adjustments to defeat Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision and defend his bantamweight title.
Merab Dvalishvili set a new UFC record with 58 total takedown attempts during his title fight against Petr Yan at UFC 333.
body: Rarely in a calendar year for the UFC is there a single combination of title fights atop the card that showcased as much pound-for-pound greatness in a single night as UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi did last weekend.

In the main event, 38-year-old Alexander Volkanoski appeared to cement the idea that he's the greatest featherweight in the sport's history as the two-time champion backed up his pre-fight prediction by stopping unbeaten Movsar Evloev inside of two rounds.

Volkanovski, who has won three straight since suffering back-to-back stoppage losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria, passed Brazilian legend Jose Aldo for the most featherweight title wins in UFC history while equaling Aldo's company mark for the most 145-pound title defenses. And if it wasn't already apparent, Volkanovski reminded fans that they were watching truly one of the greatest mixed martial artists in history ply his craft amid a period in which he's redefining what longevity looks like in the lower weight divisions.

The co-main event, on the other hand, produced P4P-worthy performances on both sides of the Octagon as two-time bantamweight titleholder Petr Yan defended his title in a against Merab Dvalishvili.

In a true "tale of two fights," Dvalishvili used his insane pace and spamming wrestling attack (which produced a new UFC record of 58 total takedown attempts) to sweep the first two rounds before the poise, pinpoint striking and cage IQ of Yan was able to rally to sweep the final three rounds and the decision.

Dvalishvili, who turns 36 in January, appeared to be in the best cardiovascular shape of his career (which is truly saying something considering his all-time great motor) and he made enough adjustments to his entry points and shooting style to give Yan plenty of fits in the early going. "The Machine" was so good in defeat, in fact, that there's an argument to be made that he would've defeated any other 135-pounder in the world on this night.
Just not Yan.

For the second straight fight, the 33-year-old Yan proved that by making calm, championship adjustments midfight, he was able to neutralize the two parts of Dvalishvili's game (his cardio and wrestling) that overwhelmed every single elite fighter in the division until their rematch last December.

Yan, who is in the midst of one of the sport's greatest comebacks after losing his title in 2020 and losing three of his next four fights immediately after, has only improved his well-rounded game in just about every aspect since his first title reign and has a strong case for consideration as the best and most accomplished bantamweight champion in UFC history.
Men's pound-for-pound rankings
1. Islam Makhachev -- Welterweight champion
Record: 29-1 | Previous ranking: No. 1

The two-division champion made history at UFC 330 in August when he broke Anderson Silva's record for consecutive wins inside the Octagon with 17 following a unanimous decision win over Ian Machado Garry. The fight pushed the 35-year-old Makhachev to the limit, however, in his lone appearance in 2026 and he was criticized for telling UFC , which created the need for a Carlos Prates-Michael Morales interim title bout at UFC 336 in Toronto.
2. Alexander Volkanovski -- Featherweight champion
Record: 29-4 | Previous ranking: No. 2

At 38, the two-time featherweight king made a respectable case for himself as fighter of the year in 2026 by packaging a January decision win over Diego Lopes in their rematch with an October return and a second-round TKO finish of unbeaten Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. Volkanovski improved to 15-1 in the UFC at 145 pounds and broke Jose Aldo's record for featherweight title wins (while equaling Aldo's mark for title defenses).
3. Petr Yan -- Bantamweight champion
Record: 21-5 | Previous ranking: No. 4

Some 10 months removed from winning back his 135-pound title in a rematch with Merab Dvalishvili, Yan squared off with "The Machine" for a third time at UFC 333 in October and delivered a thrilling performance in a unanimous decision win. Yan, 33, fell behind in the opening rounds as Dvalishvili would go on to break his own record for takedown attempts in a single fight (58). But a surge over the final three rounds saw Yan repeatedly hurt his foe while outworking him to make a strong claim for the honor of greatest bantamweight in history.
4. Joshua Van -- Flyweight champion
Record: 18-2 | Previous ranking: No. 3

Still just 24, Van is quickly becoming one of the most well-rounded and battle-tested fighters on the planet. After making key mid-fight adjustments to finish Tatsuro Taira in the fifth round of his first title defense in May, Van returned to outduel determined former champion Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331. If that isn't enough, Van has already signed on to defend his title against hard-hitting Manel Kape in the main event of UFC 336 in January.
5. Sean Strickland -- Middleweight champion
Record: 31-7 | Previous ranking: No. 5

Written off following a second title loss to Dricus du Plessis in early 2025, Strickland responded with one heck of a resurgence. First, the 35-year-old ran over red-hot Anthony Hernandez in a third-round TKO. Less than three months later, at UFC 328 in May, Strickland regained his 185-pound title by upsetting unbeaten Khamzat Chimaev via split decision. Strickland's offense might be predictable, but it's his defensive ability that makes him a tough out for everyone.
6. Justin Gaethje -- Lightweight champion
Record: 28-5 | Previous ranking: No. 6

The recent renaissance run for the 37-year-old Gaethje reached an entirely new level in June when he battered Ilia Topuria to upset his way to the 155-pound title at the White House. Gaethje's third attempt at the undisputed lightweight title turned into the biggest win in his Hall-of-Fame career. "The Highlight" has a strong case for 2026 fighter of the year honors considering he already outdueled Paddy Pimblett in January for the interim crown.
7. Ilia Topuria -- Lightweight
Record: 17-1 | Previous ranking: No. 7

Just as it looked as if Topuria was on his way to all-time great status following a trio of title knockouts over legends like Volkanovski, Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira in consecutive fights across two weight divisions, the 29-year-old was humbled in an upset loss to Justin Gaethje at the White House in June. Topuria, who snapped an 11-month layoff, suffered a pair of broken orbital bones and was unable to get up from his stool after Round 4 in a brutal brawl despite appearing to be just moments away from stopping Gaethje in Round 2.
8. Arman Tsarukyan -- Lightweight
Record: 24-3 | Previous ranking: No. 9

Following his sixth straight win in September at UFC 331, when he knocked Mauricio Ruffy out cold late in Round 1, Tsarukyan's case for a 155-pound title shot can simply no longer be denied. The native of Armenia has evolved into one of the most dangerous and well-rounded fighters in the sport and has also used his recent run of inactivity to build his star through social media on a global level. At 29, Tsarukyan is operating at the absolute peak of his powers.
9. Merab Dvalishvili -- Bantamweight
Record: 21-6 | Previous ranking: No. 8

Despite back-to-back title losses against Petr Yan over the last 10 months, including their trilogy bout at UFC 333 in October, it's hard to argue against the idea that Dvalishvili is still one of the pound-for-pound best in the world. "The Machine" showcased his exceptional cardio and broke his own record in the third Yan fight for takedowns attempted in a single fight with 58. The 35-year-old Dvalishvili likely would've defeated any other bantamweight on the planet on that night.
10. Charles Oliveira -- Lightweight
Record: 37-11 (1 NC) | Previous ranking: NR

It may not have met the definition of a true BMF title fight from the standpoint of action, but Oliveira dominated Max Holloway with his wrestling at UFC 326 in March to capture the ceremonial belt. Now 37, the Brazilian legend will defend his BMF title in December while headlining UFC 335 in Las Vegas against all-action countryman Diego Lopes as "Do Bronx" continues to seek another shot at regaining the 155-pound title.
Dropped out: Alex Pereira
Just missed: Cyril Gane, Khamzat Chimaev,Alexandre Pantoja, Pereira, Manel Kape
Women's pound-for-pound rankings
1. Valentina Shevchenko -- Flyweight
Record: 26-4-1 | Previous ranking: No. 1

Shevchenko reminded us of her greatness at UFC 322 in November 2025 by relying on her grappling to completely neutralize two-time strawweight champion Weili Zhang. But a series of injuries forced the 38-year-old to eventually vacate her 125-pound title, which puts her fighting future in question as she approaches one full year of inactivity.
2. Kayla Harrison -- Bantamweight champion
Record: 19-1 | Previous ranking: No. 2

A showdown against former champion (and former teammate) Amanda Nunes in January was delayed when Harrison pulled out just weeks before after injuring her neck and undergoing surgery. A rebooking is set for UFC 334 in November as the 36-year-old Harrison aims for the biggest win of her career amid rumors this fight could be her last.
3. Natalia Silva -- Flyweight champion
Record: 21-5-1 | Previous ranking: No. 5

Although an injury to the two-time champion Shevchenko left the 125-pound title vacant, Silva instantly filled the gap atop the division in the main event of UFC 332 in October. The native of Brazil outworked Wang Cong over five rounds and survived a late rally from the Chinese striker to win the title via decision. Silva will likely need to defeat a returning Shevchenko in 2027, however, to fully receive the respect from fans and critics as the best in the division.
4. Zhang Weili -- Strawweight/Flyweight
Record: 26-4 | Previous ranking: No. 3

The 37-year-old Zhang, a two-time strawweight champion, appears as if she will sit out all of 2026 following a November 2025 loss to Shevchenko at flyweight in her bid to become a two-division champion. Zhang, the first Chinese-born champion in UFC history, still has yet to declare which division she will make her return to although her presence would be an immediate boost to both the strawweight and flyweight title pictures.
5. Mackenzie Dern -- Strawweight champion
Record: 17-5 | Previous ranking: No. 4

It may have taken her some time to get here but Dern very much looked like a champion in her first 115-pound title defense at UFC 330 in August. Dern showcased noticeable improvements to her wrestling game and striking in a unanimous decision win over Gillian Robertson. Is a showdown against former two-time champion Zhang Weili on the horizon?
Dropped out: None
Just missed: Alexa Grasso, Tatiana Suarez, Fatima Kline, Manon Fiorot, Jasmine Jasudavicius

articles.headline: Silent Hill Remake Release Window and Other First Details Leak
keyFacts: Konami intends to release Bloober Team's remake of the original Silent Hill in 2027, according to a report from MP1st.

body: After a decade of dormancy, the Silent Hill series is back in a big way. Konami said in late 2025 that it wants to release a new Silent Hill game every year, an ambitious proposal that the publisher says it can pull off because it is already working on “many” unannounced projects. At least so far, the company has kept up its end of the bargain, with the Silent Hill 2 remake, Silent Hill f, and Silent Hill: Townfall all coming out in the last three years.

According to a report from MP1st, Konami intends to keep this impressive streak going by releasing Bloober Team's remake of the original Silent Hill in 2027. While development schedules are prone to change, it's quite possible the game will be out sometime next year.

MP1st also revealed two voice actors who will star in the remake: Gabrielle Fritz and Jade Matthew. Fritz is an English-German actor who previously appeared in games like Battlefield 2042 and The Tomorrow Children, and on TV shows such as FBI: International. As for Matthew, she appeared in Judy (2014), Suite 313, and Torchwood: The Story Continues. While MP1st Cybil Bennet, Lisa Garland, Dahlia Gillespie, Cheryl, or Alessa.
Bloober Team's Silent Hill remake was first announced in 2025

Leaker Dusk Golem previously claimed that Bloober Team has been working on the Silent Hill remake since 2022, making a 2027 release even more plausible. Konami first announced the Silent Hill remake in June 2025 following the success of Bloober’s Silent Hill 2 remake.

Beyond this, details on the game are sparse, although it seems possible that Bloober Team will once again take a comprehensive approach to the remake; the team’s Silent Hill 2 remake introduced some significant changes to its source material that, for better or worse, nearly doubled how long it took to get through the game.

Bloober Team currently has a packed release schedule. The studio is also working on DLC for Cronos: The New Dawn and Layers of Fear 3. Between the Silent Hill 2 remake and Cronos, Bloober Team has made a solid reputational comeback in recent years, after games like The Medium and 2023’s Layers of Fear left a sour taste. With Silent Hill and the recent release of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Konami has marked its own unlikely return.

articles.headline: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
keyFacts: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding Nairobi is a city of rivers, streams and almost six million people.
For weeks, Kenya's bustling capital has braced for potentially catastrophic floods, as forecasters predict the strongest El Niño event on record this winter.
Globally, this year's Super El Niño will likely peak in November or December and continue into early 2027.
body: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
Nairobi is a city of rivers, streams and almost six million people.

For weeks, Kenya's bustling capital has braced for potentially catastrophic floods, as forecasters predict the strongest El Niño event on record this winter. Globally, this year's Super El Niño will likely peak in November or December and continue into early 2027. But Nairobi isn't just watching and waiting.

On a sunny October day near the city center, a team of workers in reflective vests shovels dirt and clears debris from the bank of a river. It's unseasonably hot — and hot days usually suggest there's an unusually strong rainy season ahead.

"The best thing to do is to be prepared," says Alex Oyando, a 30-year-old worker. "These drainage troughs are full of different things. When we remove the dirt, the water can flow — and it prevents flooding."

Nairobi frequently experiences catastrophic flash floods. More than 100 people died during rain-induced flash floods last March, and residents have pressured Kenya's government to do more to prevent these disasters in the future.
Reporting for El Niño duty

As part of the preparations, Nairobi's county government has mobilized the "Green Army," a youth-employment program of more than 4,000 people. While generally assigned to trash pickups and city greening projects, the workers have been out in full force to prepare for El

Niño, clearing drainages and dismantling illegal structures like food stalls. These buildings are generally constructed by the community without government permits and are at an increased risk of collapsing during natural disasters.

Earlier this month, Oyando and his colleagues widened a drainage ditch that runs along a busy road lined with stalls selling clothing. Piles of fabric, plastic bottles and other litter often build up in the stream, triggering flash floods.
While the pay isn't as much as he could make elsewhere, Oyando admits, the shifts are manageable and not too grueling.
"It's something that gives me an opportunity to make a living," he says.

Many of Oyando's colleagues live or grew up in Nairobi's low-income neighborhoods, which are the hardest hit by flash floods. Aging drainage infrastructure and clogged waterways can cause stormwater to build up. When it rains, he says, it's not unusual for his street to fill with water and flood his home.

"The infrastructure we've had in place for decades was tailored for a population of not more than 2 million people," says Bramwell Simiyu, the chief officer of disaster management for Nairobi's county government. "We're now talking about a daytime population of close to 7 million."
A $385 million remedy

Kenya's federal government has put in place a $385 million plan to widen Nairobi's waterways, build affordable housing and improve the city's trash pickup and sewer system by the end of 2027. In addition, the program supports a national youth employment program called Climate WorX, which is working with the Green Army on El Niño preparations.
Now, Simiyu says, the county is preparing supplies and evacuation centers for the rainy season.
"We're also preparing for a worst-case scenario, where up to about 20,000 households may be affected — mostly in the low -income settlements," Simiyu said.
Controversial demolitions

In these settlements, the demolition of illegally built structures, such as food hawker stalls, has caused an outcry. Tobias Sifuna, a supervisor for Green Army teams in the Kamukunji area of Nairobi, says it's a necessary step.
"These are small kiosks that are built illegally, by the community — without the authorization from the county government," Sifuna said.
But nearby communities rely on them, for income and for daily shopping.
Wycliffe Ochieng, a 32-year-old fruit vendor, says many workers in central Nairobi now have nowhere to buy an affordable hot lunch during the day.
"Now, we have to sleep without food because we can't afford it," Ochieng says.

When the county government destroys the shops, it's the community that feels the loss — whether or not the floods eventually come. But it's these neighborhoods that were hit the hardest by the floods during the last rainy season. Ochieng himself had to sleep outdoors, because he could not reach his home in the floodwaters.
"This place, it's like an ocean when it's raining," Ochieng says. "When the flood came, all the food stalls were swept away."

His friend, a woman who owned a food stall, died as she tried to escape. He lost his own stand, a small grocery, as well. He struggled to rebuild his business in a new neighborhood, where customers no longer knew him by reputation.
"After the flood I really suffered. It was hard to put food on the table," Ochieng says.
He says he hopes the county can do more to prevent flooding and safeguard livelihoods. There are only so many times he can rebuild his life from scratch.
"We are all scared. I fear if El Niño comes, I won't come back again."
For stories about life in our changing world, subscribe to NPR's Global Health newsletter.

articles.headline: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
keyFacts: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or trophy at a ceremony held in London on Monday.
Lamine Yamal finished third and Kylian Mbappe came in second for the award judging the 2025-26 season.
Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last season and became the first Bundesliga player to win since 1996.
body: To most Bayern Munich fans under the age of 40, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was the club CEO who regularly spoke his mind. Fans with longer memories, or a better grasp of Bavarian football history, recall Rummenigge as one of the club's all-time great players. He was also the last Bayern man to win the Ballon d'Or — in 1981. The last Bundesliga player to win was Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer, in 1996.
That long drought ended on Monday, with Harry Kane, born 12 years after Rummenigge's win, picking up the 2026 trophy at a ceremony held, as a one-off, in his native London.
"I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special,” he said on stage.
Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane later told British sports streaming plaftorm DAZN.

Lamine Yamal, the prodigious Barcelona and Spain forward who won the Euros at 16, finished third. At the end of the 2025-26 season, on which the award is judged, Yamal won the World Cup with Spain as well as the La Liga title. Kylian Mbappe came in second.
Kane's career not just measured in numbers

Kane's 73 goals for club and country last season made for a strong case, and the Bundesliga's most expensive signing of all time has already racked up 156 goals in 159 games for the serial German champions. But it's not just the numbers that tell the story, according to his club coach.

"People in England saw him as a goalscorer during his time playing there," Vincent Kompany said of Kane last season. "We've seen other qualities too, such as his footballing intelligence. We can appreciate that now — it was perhaps somewhat underestimated in England. He's like a fine wine that improves with age. I also enjoy that aspect of his game."

Kane continues to improve at 33, a point when many footballers start to regress. Though he is helped by being more reliant on guile and technique than pace, Kane's professionalism is key to staying at the top, according to his Bayern teammate Serge Gnabry.

"He always has the right attitude, always leads the way and sets the tone," Gnabry said ahead of Bayern's 2-2 draw in the Champions League against Arsenal last week. "He never strays from his path, helps the team with his performance and is a top-tier player."

Kane scored a penalty in that match and provided a sensational pass from which Alphonso Davies scored Bayern's opener, another reminder of his all-round game. "The pass was one of my best ones," Kane said after the match. "I knew Phonzy [Davies] would be able to get there with his speed. Whatever I can do to help the team, I'll do. At the moment, it seems to be with assists more than goals."
Kane's 'greatest strength'

That attitude has been with Kane from the start. His first-ever coach, Dave Bricknell, from Ridgeway Rovers, an amateur club in northeast London, told DW after Kane joined Bayern from Spurs in 2023: "Harry's mentality is his greatest strength. He doesn't let anything worry him. If he misses a chance, he doesn't care — he will go and score from another chance."

His England coach, Thomas Tuchel, has also emphasized Kane's leadership. "He is the first one to push everyone, and that is his mindset, and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills, Tuchel said in September as Kane extended his England goal-scoring record against the Czech Republic. "He is a complete package."

There are detractors who point to perceived "stat-padding," or scoring against inferior opponents in international qualifiers and in the Bundesliga, where there are fewer elite teams and a lot less money, than in England. Though Kane's ratio of 213 goals in 320 games in the Premier League is a little off his Bundesliga stats, it bears comparison with any other player in the history of the league.

Kane winning the award is also a boost in profile for the Bundesliga, which has been unable to keep pace, both commercially and on the pitch, with other top European leagues of late, particularly the Premier League and La Liga.

Winning it in a league outside of England or Spain perhaps makes Kane's feat even greater. Other than Ousmane Dembele, who won it last year after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League win, and Lionel Messi, a serial Ballon d'Or winner, the last player to take the Ballon d'Or for a season played outside England or Spain was was Kaka at AC Milan in 2007, when Italy's Serie A was considered a stronger league.

Kane's career hasn't been straightforward, something he admitted in his speech. After signing his first senior contract with Spurs in July 2010, he was sent out on various loans to lower league sides between 2011-2013 without ever making a huge impression.

"My journey wasn't straightforward. I wasn't the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs, I had a lot of loan moves, I had to fight my way to be the very best right now, and I hope that can give you determination as well," Kane said in his speech.
Domestic trophies won but international success eludes
For former teammate Jermain Defoe, who also coached Kane at Spurs, those experiences were formative.

"You have to show a resilience. It's not easy when you go out on loan, it can feel like you're being rejected by the club that you are at, which isn't the case," he told DW in 2023, before adding that Kane's ability was always clear.

"When he joined up with the [Tottenham] first team, you could see the potential," Defoe said. "He was always a good finisher, always hit the ball clean. … With Harry you already knew, he had that natural instinct and always felt comfortable in front of goal."

Those goals have, after a failure to win a trophy in England, led to two Bundesliga titles and a German Cup. But success with England remains elusive after a 2026 World Cup exit in the semifinals. Kane will be 35 by the time of the next Euros, in the UK and Ireland in 2028, and has a deal with Bayern until the following year. His form since joining Bayern suggests that he could get better still.
Edited by: Jonathan Harding
This article was first published on October 22, 2026. It was updated on October 27 after Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Benn’s future in the sport is up in the air after he fell to a brutal two-round demolition defeat to Ryan Garcia in his step-up to fight for a world title.
